"Come see about me" is a well-known musical refrain, most famously recorded by **The Supremes** in 1964 and written by the Motown songwriting trio Holland–Dozier–Holland. It also appears as a prominent track by **Nicki Minaj** on her 2018 album *Queen*.[1][2][3]

## The Motown Classic

Recorded by The Supremes and led by Diana Ross, the 1964 single became the group's third consecutive number-one hit on the Billboard Hot 100.[4][5]

- The song features an upbeat, driving Motown tempo arranged by the Funk Brothers.[2]
- The narrative centers on romantic longing and vulnerability, as the narrator pleads for an estranged partner to return and reconcile.[6][2]
- The contrast between melancholy lyrics and energetic rhythm is a hallmark of Holland–Dozier–Holland's signature production style.[7][2]

## Modern Interpretations

Nicki Minaj released an emotional R&B ballad under the same title in 2018.[3]

- The track explores themes of regret, personal growth, and asking an ex-partner for another chance after drifting apart.[8][3]
- Rather than a rapid soul beat, it relies on a slower tempo focusing on the difficulty of maintaining relationships amidst high-profile careers.[3]

Official lyrics and audio streams for both tracks can be found on major music platforms such as Apple Music and Genius.[1][3]
